clue.text: Slush — it sent men reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about, so the three words it follows are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gushing remark about a woman who has left men staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' rearranges IT SENT MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slush is mawkish, sugary feeling, the soppy sense of the word.

clue.text: At university, president raged about this promotion

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of raged are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: A college head flew into a rage over being moved up a rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal on 'raged', not a container; 'At' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank or grade is a promotion.

clue.text: Grandee with commandant, if in Georgia may start heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OC, Officer Commanding, is a commandant
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: start points to just the opening letter of the word may

explanation.surface: A nobleman and his commanding officer may set off northwards if they reach Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes M from 'may'; 'heading north' turns OC IF IN GA M upwards to give the Italian-style grandee.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a Venetian nobleman, hence any person of high rank.

clue.text: Synonymous of madness

parts.note: the phrase points to an animal named in the simile for wild craziness, so it stands for being mad

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'mad as a ...' completes with this spring animal, famous for wild boxing behaviour in its breeding season.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial simile for lunacy uses this spring animal from Alice in Wonderland, so it is a byword for crazy behaviour.

clue.text: Forehead's well covered by some topees

indicators.note: the answer is completely enclosed by the letters of the words some topees

explanation.surface: Pith helmets shade the brow nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is'. Topees are sun helmets; METOPE is a rare word for forehead, more usually an architectural panel.
explanation.definitionFit: Metope is an old anatomical term for the brow.

clue.text: Sandman called? Came with soot, instead!

indicators.note: instead suggests the letters of came and soot are replaced by another arrangement of them

explanation.surface: The sandman was expected but a chimney sweep turned up covered in soot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead' rearranges CAME SOOT. If the sandman has called you are asleep, here pushed to deep unconsciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit from the sandman means sleep, and being out cold in a deep stupor is the extreme of that.

clue.text: Damaged petal of sweet pea? It's a bean caper!

parts.note: harm is damage done, the clue's past participle stretched to the condition
the ala is a wing petal of a pea flower

explanation.surface: A gardener's mishap with a sweet pea petal is treated as a bean prank.
explanation.walkthrough: Pea-family flowers have two side petals called alae (wings). 'Damaged' has to give HARM loosely. Harmala and the bean caper are plants of the same caltrop family.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmala, Syrian rue, is a plant related to the bean caper in the caltrop family.

clue.text: Progress from the right in turn

indicators.note: from the right puts the letter for right at the start, the place the reading begins

parts.note: to evolve is to progress or develop

explanation.surface: Moving forward from the right, one takes a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to rotate, going round as a wheel does.

clue.text: To make amends after I barge in on former head

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: to barge in is to push into something, so the letter I goes inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Apologising after crashing a barge into the old boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge in' is the insertion signal: the barge is not a boat here, and 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to atone or pay the penalty for it.

clue.text: Polish politician — one to gallivant about

indicators.note: about here means around, so the words for one and gallivant go on either side of the politician

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rove is to wander or gallivant
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician from Poland wanders about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb to refine. 'about' works as a container, wrapping one and gallivant round the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish work is to refine and better it.

clue.text: City investor on top form's holding

indicators.note: the words investor on top hold the answer within them, as in a form's contents

explanation.surface: A financier at the top of his game.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the run from inves(TOR ON TO)p.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: Split up with one friend, though not entirely?

parts.note: to part is to split up or separate
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Broke up with a single pal, but not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Partially means only in part, to a limited degree.

clue.text: Space left by molar he pulled out?

indicators.note: pulled out of shape, the letters of molar and he are reshuffled

explanation.surface: The gap a dentist leaves after extracting a man's back tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' rearranges MOLAR HE. The gap is the opening in a garment for the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armhole is the gap in a garment for the arm to pass through.

clue.text: Idiom ref used to describe qualifier

indicators.note: used here means reworked, so the letters of idiom and ref are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, short for referee

explanation.surface: A referee's turn of phrase, used to describe a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges IDIOM REF.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a modifier is a word that qualifies or limits another.

clue.text: Being under the influence, was unsteady on one's feet

explanation.surface: Drunk, and tottering as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swayed is to be influenced by persuasion; to sway is also to rock or lurch from side to side.

clue.text: A different rodent from rat we love

indicators.note: different signals the letters of rat we love made into a different word

explanation.surface: A rodent that is not like the rats we adore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges RAT WE LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole is a riverbank rodent, a small mammal of British waterways.

clue.text: Drain they dread re-entering

indicators.note: re-entering suggests the letters of they and dread go back in a new order

explanation.surface: A sewer that people fear going back into.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-entering' rearranges THEY DREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain something of moisture is to dry it out, removing its water.

clue.text: Army officer briefly suffering with ache — located in the ear

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: Col is the short form of colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A colonel is in pain with earache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges COL and ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear, sitting deep within the hearing organ.

clue.text: Sea-creatures circle firm beach where fruit is to be found

definitions.text: where fruit is to be found

indicators.note: the sea creatures go round the other piece, enclosing it as a ring does

parts.note: orcs are mythical sea monsters, also killer whales
a hard is a firm sloping foreshore used as a landing place

explanation.surface: Sea creatures gather around a solid shore where fruit is found.
explanation.walkthrough: A hard is a nautical term for a firm beach or landing place.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchards are plantations of fruit trees.

clue.text: Nervousness apparent though capital returns from trading registered initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words trading and registered
returns means the word for the capital comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A city's trading figures show jitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives TR; 'returns' turns ROME into EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a trembling or quiver, visible nerves.

clue.text: Poem — translation of an ode finally acceptable by monarch

indicators.note: finally puts the letter for acceptable at the end

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

indicators.note: translation turns the words an ode into another form, here a reordering of their letters

parts.note: U means socially acceptable, upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A poem translated from an ode is finally approved by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges AN ODE into ONDEA. U for acceptable is the upper-class label of the 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain.

clue.text: Notes I'm ordered what's contrary to sixteen down!

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of notes and I'm are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A memo saying I'm instructed to do the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges NOTES I'M. Sixteen down is DEHYDRATE, so the opposite is to dampen.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something damp is the reverse of drying it out.

clue.text: Sail, following navigational guide into the interior

indicators.note: the interior means the inside, so the word into is placed within the guide

parts.note: a map guides navigation

explanation.surface: Setting sail using a chart to head inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the interior' is the container signal for the word 'into'; a maintop is strictly a platform on the mainmast.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the top of the mainmast, and by extension the topsail rigged there.

clue.text: The scholarly type it rarely improved

indicators.note: improved suggests reworking, so the letters of it and rarely are rearranged

explanation.surface: The academic kind seldom gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improved' rearranges IT RARELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes something bookish, concerned with learning and letters.

clue.text: Truthfully, it's no longer denied

indicators.note: no longer in its original form, so the letters of denied are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is true, it can't be refuted any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' rearranges DENIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is used to confirm a statement, meaning really or in truth.

clue.text: Novel I lengthen to edify

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of I and lengthen are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Making a book longer to instruct readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book, but it means new and rearranges I LENGTHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct and improve the mind, to inform.

clue.text: He finds water even more delightful

explanation.surface: A dowser who is more heavenly still.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser locates underground springs with a rod; divine means heavenly or lovely, and its comparative is the second sense.

clue.text: Put back all that's left of the mineral

parts.note: the rest is the remainder, all that remains
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Replace whatever remains of the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore is to return something to its place or condition.

clue.text: Burbot made another fish look petulant

parts.note: an eel is a fish
to pout is to look sulky or petulant

explanation.surface: A burbot made a second fish sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: The burbot is a freshwater fish also known by this alternative name.

clue.text: Cast net around vessel, being thus equipped

indicators.note: the word for casting a net is placed around the vessel

parts.note: to cast a net is to have fished
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Throwing a net round a boat to get properly kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; 'vessel' wants to be a boat but is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnished room is fitted out with furniture, so the word means provided or supplied.
